answers.answer: A clearing is ruled by the player with the most combined warriors and buildings; ordinary ties mean nobody rules. How Eyrie ties, tokens, and the Vagabond pawn affect rule is not stated.
answers.evidence: Special Rules & Edge Cases: ‘most combined warriors and buildings’; ‘Ties mean no one rules.’

answers.answer: A normal move goes from a clearing to an adjacent connected clearing and requires ruling either the origin or destination. Repeated movement by the same warriors and whether rivers count as paths are not stated.
answers.evidence: Shared Rules for All Factions—Movement: ‘Move warriors from one clearing to an adjacent connected clearing’ and rule the origin or destination.

answers.answer: Defenders may play matching-suit Ambush cards at the start of battle to deal 2 hits before dice. The attacker rolls two dice; high die gives attacker hits and low die defender hits, with maximum hits limited by warriors present. Warriors are removed before tokens/buildings, and each removed building or token scores 1 VP for the attacker. Foiling, early ending, further extra hits, and other removal details are not stated.
answers.evidence: Shared Rules—Battle and Special Rules—Ambush Cards; summary says ‘Remove warriors first, then tokens/buildings.’

answers.answer: Crafting uses cards matching the suits of clearings where the faction has crafting pieces. Exact costs, reusing a crafting piece, what happens if a supply item is absent, and duplicate persistent effects are not stated.
answers.evidence: Shared Rules—Crafting: ‘Spend cards matching the suits of clearings where you have crafting pieces … to craft items or activate card effects.’

answers.answer: A Dominance card changes the player's win condition to controlling 3 specific clearings at the start of their next Birdsong; other players may also adopt Dominance. The VP threshold and timing for activation, which suit wins, and whether an activated card can be replaced or discarded are not stated.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: ‘play a Dominance card to change their win condition to controlling 3 specific clearings at the start of their next Birdsong.’

answers.answer: The summary does not explain what happens to a Dominance card spent for its suit or how another player can take it, including a bird Dominance card.
answers.evidence: Dominance is only described as a card played to change the win condition; card disposition and taking it are not described.

answers.answer: The general setup says to shuffle the shared deck, deal 3 cards to each player, place item tokens on ruin spaces and in the supply, and follow each faction's unique setup. Two-player deck changes, two-player hand size, exact ruins/item setup, and faction setup order are not stated.
answers.evidence: Setup: ‘Shuffle the shared deck and deal 3 cards to each player’; ‘Place item tokens on the map's ruin spaces and in the supply’; ‘Follow the faction-specific setup instructions.’

answers.answer: The Keep's restrictions and permissions, Field Hospitals, and whether the Keep can be rebuilt are not stated.
answers.evidence: No Keep or Field Hospitals rules appear in the supplied summary.

answers.answer: The summary lists Marquise actions as Battle, March, Recruit, Build, and Overwork, with 3 actions plus 1 bonus action per bird card. It does not state their required order, how many moves a March includes, a Recruit limit, or the Overwork cost beyond spending a card to produce extra wood.
answers.evidence: Marquise de Cat—Daylight: ‘Spend actions to Battle, March (move), Recruit … Build … Overwork (spend a card to produce extra wood). Limited to 3 actions + 1 bonus action per bird card.’

answers.answer: The Marquise builds using wood. It scores VP by building workshops, sawmills, and recruiters, with escalating VP for each new building of a type. The rule requirement, wood network details, track selection, and exact scoring values are not stated.
answers.evidence: Marquise de Cat: ‘Build (place buildings using wood)’ and scores VP by building the three structure types, with ‘escalating VP.’

answers.answer: In Birdsong the Eyrie adds 1–2 cards to the Decree. The no-roost recovery placement requirement is not stated.
answers.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties—Birdsong: ‘Add 1-2 cards to the Decree.’

answers.answer: The Eyrie resolves Decree columns in Recruit, Move, Battle, Build order; cards force actions in matching-suit clearings. The summary does not describe within-column ordering or the restrictions on building roosts.
answers.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties—Daylight: ‘Resolve the Decree in order: Recruit, Move, Battle, Build roosts. Each card … forces actions in matching-suit clearings.’

answers.answer: On Turmoil, the Eyrie loses VP equal to the number of bird cards in the Decree, removes all warriors and buildings except roosts, chooses a new leader, and resets the Decree. The summary does not say what happens to Viziers or how the rest of the turn proceeds.
answers.evidence: Special Rules—Turmoil: ‘lose VP equal to the number of bird cards in the Decree, remove all warriors and buildings except roosts, choose a new leader, and reset the Decree.’

answers.answer: The summary says other players must give the Alliance a card when entering or battling in sympathetic clearings. It does not state the precise trigger timing, which card is paid, or what happens if the player lacks a matching card or the supporter stack is full.
answers.evidence: Woodland Alliance: ‘Other players must give the Alliance a card when entering or battling in sympathetic clearings.’

answers.answer: In Birdsong the Alliance may Revolt by spending supporters to place a base and warriors and remove all enemy pieces from a clearing, or Spread Sympathy by spending supporters to place sympathy tokens. The summary does not specify action timing/order beyond the Birdsong listing, eligible clearings, exact costs, or martial-law effects.
answers.evidence: Woodland Alliance—Birdsong: ‘Revolt (spend supporters to place a base and warriors, removing all enemy pieces from a clearing) or Spread Sympathy (spend supporters to place sympathy tokens).’

answers.answer: Training spends cards from the supporters stack to add officers. Organize is described as drawing cards. What losing a base does to supporters and officers is not stated.
answers.evidence: Woodland Alliance: ‘Train (spend cards from supporters to add officers)’; Evening lists ‘organize (draw cards).’

answers.answer: The Vagabond refreshes exhausted items and can Slip without ruling. Normal Move exhausts a boot. In Evening, the Vagabond may rest in a forest to repair all items or draw cards. Hostile destination rules and any other details of refresh, Slip, or Evening drawing are not stated.
answers.evidence: Vagabond—Birdsong: ‘Refresh exhausted items, slip (move without ruling)’; Daylight: ‘Move (exhaust boot)’; Evening: ‘Rest in forest (repair all items) or draw cards.’

answers.answer: Explore a ruin by exhausting a torch. A Quest discards 2 matching-suit cards for VP. The summary does not state Repair's cost or effect, rewards for exploring or quests, or which item sides are involved.
answers.evidence: Vagabond—Daylight: ‘Explore ruins (exhaust torch)’ and ‘Quest (discard 2 matching-suit cards for VP).’

answers.answer: A faction becomes Hostile when the Vagabond removes 3 of its warriors, and aiding factions improves relations. The summary does not say when Infamy is scored, whether Aid can undo Hostility, or what Strike targets.
answers.evidence: Special Rules—Hostile/Allied Relations: ‘Removing 3 of a faction's warriors makes them Hostile. Aiding factions improves relations.’

answers.answer: The Vagabond may form a coalition with the lowest-scoring player and shares that player's win condition. The summary does not state eligibility beyond this, timing, a VP requirement, partner-selection procedure, or how a Hostile partner changes the coalition.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: ‘The Vagabond may form a coalition with the lowest-scoring player, sharing that player's win condition.’
